figures.finding: The Faroe Islands refund 25% of a production's spend there under the 2017 rebate act, to bring foreign productions to the islands: the budget sets aside DKK 200,000 a year, the ceiling was raised to 5 million in 2023, and a production must spend at least four times the rebate in the Faroes (local wages, goods and services, food, vehicle and equipment hire).

value.minSpend: 4x the rebate in the Faroe Islands

figures.applies: Faroe Islands; as Nordisk Film & TV Fond reported in May 2018; current terms not confirmed.

sources.said: I 2017 varð lógin um afturbering samtykt. Á fíggjarlógini eru 200.000 DKK settar av árliga til endamálið. Í 2023 varð samtykt at hækka loftið til 5 mill. Afturberingin er 25%. Fyri at fáa afturbering skal ein framleiðsla leggja í minsta lagi fýra ferðir afturberingarupphæddina eftir seg í Føroyum. … Afturberingin er ein tileggjan til at fáa útlendskar framleiðslur at gera upptøkur og framleiða í Føroyum.
with the recently introduced 25% tax incentive to attract foreign shoots, and a new generation of directors and producers.

figures.finding: The Faroese Film Institute opened in 2017-18 with DKK 1 million a year from the Ministry of Trade to attract foreign productions and market the islands, and an extra DKK 2 million from the Ministry of Culture towards film production support.
figures.applies: Faroe Islands; as reported at the institute's opening (November 2017).

sources.said: With an annual budget of DKK 1 million provided for by the local Ministry of Trade to attract foreign productions and market the Faroe Islands internationally, and an extra DKK 2 million from the Ministry of Culture towards film production support, the new Faroese Film Institute is now open for business.

figures.finding: Filmshúsið and the Betri group fund Faroese film projects with DKK 2 million for 2026-2028: at most DKK 500,000 for a larger Faroese film project, DKK 75,000 for project development and DKK 130,000 for short-film development; the 2026 deadline is 1 October.
